title: This Bhoot Chaturdashi, dare to go ghost spotting in Kolkata
excerpt: Kolkata has no shortage of ghost stories, but what happens when you step beyond the folklore and follow the trail yourself? This Bhoot Chaturdashi, we joined paranormal investigators on a ghost hunt, visiting locations steeped in eerie accounts and unexplained occurrences.
content:
Kolkata has no shortage of ghost stories, but what happens when you step beyond the folklore and follow the trail yourself? This Bhoot Chaturdashi, we joined paranormal investigators on a ghost hunt, visiting locations steeped in eerie accounts and unexplained occurrences.

With EMF meters, thermal cameras and voice recorders in tow, we got a glimpse of what goes into investigating the supernatural, where every strange sound or unusual reading is met with curiosity, caution and a fair amount of scepticism. From colonial-era cemeteries to old mansions and metro stations, we explore the stories that continue to haunt the city.

Pics : Anindya Saha

Behind the scenes of a paranormal investigation

For Detectives of Supernatural (DOS), an investigation begins with historical research, local accounts and eyewitness testimonies.

The team comprises founder Devraj Sanyal, researcher Ishita Das Sanyal, technical head Anirban Das and field investigator and legal advisor Ayush Mazumdar. "We study a location's history and the circumstances surrounding alleged activity before conducting a preliminary inspection, identifying environmental factors and dividing the area into zones," says Devraj.

The team looks for unusual sounds, visual anomalies and temperature fluctuations while ruling out logical explanations first.

"An EMF spike could be caused by concealed wiring, a thermal anomaly by air circulation, and an unexplained sound by structural movement or animals. Just because we cannot explain something today doesn't mean science cannot explain it tomorrow. Healthy scepticism is the foundation of paranormal research," says Ishita. Meanwhile, Subhamoy Mukherjee, co-founder of Bengal Paranormal Society, says his childhood interest in the subject led him to establish the group using his own funds.

"We have investigated several locations and built an equipment collection, much of it sourced from the US. Unlike those who stage videos, whatever we share is based on actual investigations. We do not fake content for views," he says.

We don’t walk into a place looking for a ghost. We walk in looking for answers. We study its history, test every sound, every cold spot and every reading, and only when every normal explanation fails do we consider the paranormal.

- Devraj Sanyal, founder and lead Investigator of Detectives of Supernatural

The gadgets that accompany a ghost hunt

A paranormal investigation involves an array of specialised equipment. The DOS team uses EMF meters to monitor electromagnetic variations, thermal cameras and parabolic thermometers to detect temperature changes, and digital voice recorders to capture possible Electronic Voice Phenomena (EVP).

Their kit also includes infrared and full-spectrum cameras, laser grids to track visual movement, motion sensors, REM Pods, environmental sensors and data loggers to monitor temperature, humidity and atmospheric pressure.

Toxic gas detectors help rule out gases such as carbon monoxide and methane as possible causes of unusual experiences. While DOS uses several such instruments, Bengal Paranormal Society sources much of its equipment from abroad, particularly the US, and continues to expand its collection.

DOS also develops some of its own equipment. However, a strange reading is not proof of paranormal activity. As Anirban Das of DOS explains, "Instruments provide data; interpretation requires investigation."

Kolkata's ghost stories: Between history and folklore

Kolkata’s ghost stories draw on colonial-era tragedies, forgotten histories and Bengali folklore. Author Abhirup Dhar believes that many supposedly haunted places have stories rooted in real human experience.

“Behind many of the city’s supposedly haunted locations, there is often a very real history of displacement, political intrigue and forgotten lives,” he says, citing South Park Street Cemetery, Hastings House, the National Library and the Writers’ Building.

Ishita Das Sanyal, director and researcher at Detectives of Supernatural (DOS), also stresses the importance of examining the history and circumstances behind reported paranormal activity rather than relying only on popular accounts. DOS field investigator Ayush Mazumdar points to places such as Putul Bari, but cautions that it is a residential property and its occupants must not be disturbed. Dhar also highlights lesser-known tales linked to Putul Bari, also called the House of Dolls, in Shobhabazar, Imli ka Peer in Diamond Harbour, Metiabruz, and a Jewish cemetery in the Kankurgachi–Narkeldanga area. He hopes Bhoot Chaturdashi will renew interest in Bengal’s indigenous spirits such as Petni, Shakchunni, Brahmadaitya and Skandhakata. “Each of these figures has a story behind it, but we have not explored these legends enough. It is time we revisited them,” he says.

People imagine a ghost on every visit. Mostly, our work is research, observation and documentation. Some nights, absolutely nothing happens, and that is part of the job.

- Anirban Das, Technical Head and investigator of Detectives of Supernatural

PLACES TO EXPLORE KOLKATA'S SPOOKY SIDE

  • South Park Street Cemetery: Dating back to 1767, it is associated with colonial-era legends. DOS says its equipment has registered unusual readings near certain tombs.
  • National Library (Belvedere House): Stories of unexplained footsteps and the legendary Lady Metcalfe surround the property.
  • Hastings House: Associated with Warren Hastings, it has a legend of a ghostly carriage returning in search of missing belongings.
  • Rabindra Sarobar Metro: Stories of strange sightings and unexplained occurrences have circulated around the station.
  • Putul Bari, North Kolkata: The residential mansion is associated with tales of tragic deaths, laughter and anklet sounds. Visitors should respect its occupants.
  • Diamond Harbour: An ancient tamarind tree, Imli ka Peer, is linked to local folklore.
  • Metiabruz: Stories of ghostly royal processions and music are associated with Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.

Paranormal research requires scientific grounding. While mainstream science cannot accept these events, quantum science, which sometimes challenges conventional theories, may offer answers

– Suvojyoti Roy Chowdhury, paranormal researcher

BEFORE YOU SET OUT ON A SPOOKY TRAIL

  • Obtain permission before entering private, government-owned or restricted properties.
  • Never explore abandoned structures without authorisation and a safety assessment.
  • Avoid going alone, especially at night.
  • Carry a torch, charged phone, first-aid kit and emergency supplies.
  • Stay away from unstable floors, open wells, abandoned lifts and exposed electrical installations.
  • Watch out for snakes, insects and other animals.
  • Avoid locations known for anti-social activity.
  • Do not trespass, disturb religious sites or damage heritage structures.
  • Respect residential properties and their occupants.

People are often fascinated by the spooky stories surrounding Kolkata, but exploring them first-hand is a completely different experience. We want people to look beyond the legends and understand the history and mystery behind these places

Subhamoy Mukherjee, co-founder of Bengal Paranormal Society
